summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a complex medical history including kidney and pancreas transplants, mechanical mitral valve replacement, systolic heart failure, and end-stage renal disease was transferred for further management after an initial admission for weakness and pneumonia. She presented with chronic epigastric pain, now thought to be related to mesenteric ischemia in the setting of extensive vascular calcifications, and was managed with increased ranitidine, initiation of omeprazole, and lorazepam at bedtime for symptom control. Pneumonia was treated with a full course of levofloxacin and resolved. An elevated troponin was attributed to demand ischemia, with stress testing showing fixed perfusion defects and an ejection fraction of 21%, stable from baseline. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure was managed by restarting torsemide, leading to improved volume status. Her INR fluctuated from subtherapeutic to therapeutic with warfarin adjustment and a brief heparin drip. She remained stable on immunosuppressive therapy and was discharged home with follow-up plans in cardiology, gastroenterology, and nephrology.
problems: Subendocardial infarction, initial episode of care
Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Heart valve replaced by other means
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
